newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl praises EU's founding fathers, urges reform.
newsitem.headline: Kohl praises EU's founding fathers, urges reform.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Tuesday praised the European leaders of 40 years ago for their foresight in signing the Treaty of Rome and called for renewed efforts to fit the continent for the challenges of the future.
Kohl said the treaty, signed by six governments in 1957 to create the European Economic Community, had paved the way for decades of peace, freedom, prosperity and social security.

In a statement, he said the founding of the EEC as well as the European Atomic Energy Community in Rome had also given Germany an "historic chance to help shape the unification of our continent as an equal partner in the family of European nations".
Kohl, widely regarded as the driving force for integration among today's politicians, said Europe must develop further but would not become a centralised superstate.

"For me, one thing goes without saying: The Europe of the future will not be a centralised, uniform state, it will build on the principle of subsidiarity, respect national and regional traditions and promote cultural diversity," he said.
Kohl said today's European Union needed to be both deepened -- through reforms due to be agreed at a summit in Amsterdam in June -- and then widened by the admission of new members.

"We need a strong European Union which is capable of action so that we can take in as new members those countries of central and southeastern Europe which are ready," he said. "The European Union will not be an exclusive club."
